The widening of the 90% confidence intervals at each successive horizon reflects the inherent increase in uncertainty as we project further into the future. While the 90% confidence intervals capture a wide range of expected outcomes, specific high-impact, low-probability events could certainly push the actual value beyond these stated boundaries. On the upside, a sudden, significant positive development—such as an unexpected technological breakthrough relevant to the variable, a major economic stimulus package, or a sudden surge in demand not currently factored into baseline models—could cause the value to climb significantly above 131.51 within a month. Conversely, severe negative shocks like a major geopolitical crisis, an unforeseen natural disaster impacting global supply chains, a sudden economic recession, or adverse regulatory changes could precipitate a sharp decline, potentially pushing the value below 109.49. These "black swan" events, by their very nature, are difficult to quantify and are not typically contained within standard probabilistic forecasts, but they represent real risks that could materially alter the future trajectory.
